sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Detailed study guide and resources for Judicial System: Law Commission are currently being prepared. Check back soon for comprehensive explanations, summary diagrams, and expert preparation recommendations.

Key Dimensions of Study:

  • Definition, scope, and foundational theories.
  • Relevance to General Studies Paper & Contemporary contexts.
  • Core applications and structural framework.

practiceQuestions.q: Under which Charter Act was the First Law Commission of British India established?
practiceQuestions.sol: The First Law Commission of British India was established under the Charter Act of 1833, which also centralized the legislative powers of the Government of India and added a law member to the Governor-General's Council. [Primary Reference: Charter Act of 1833 / Bipan Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence]

practiceQuestions.q: Who was appointed as the Chairman of the First Law Commission of British India?
practiceQuestions.sol: Lord Thomas Babington Macaulay was appointed as the first Law Member of the Governor-General-in-Council and headed the First Law Commission, which laid the groundwork for the Indian Penal Code (IPC). [Primary Reference: Charter Act of 1833 / Indian Legal History]

practiceQuestions.q: When was the First Law Commission of independent India established?
practiceQuestions.sol: The first Law Commission of independent India was established in 1955 under the chairmanship of Mr. M.C. Setalvad, who was also the first Attorney General of India. [Primary Reference: Ministry of Law and Justice, Government of India]

practiceQuestions.q: Who was the Chairman of the First Law Commission of independent India?
practiceQuestions.sol: M.C. Setalvad served as the Chairman of the First Law Commission of independent India from 1955 to 1958. [Primary Reference: Law Commission of India Reports]

practiceQuestions.q: Is the Law Commission of India a statutory body or a non-statutory body created by an executive resolution?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Law Commission of India is neither a constitutional nor a statutory body; rather, it is an executive body established by an order of the Ministry of Law and Justice for a fixed tenure. [Primary Reference: Ministry of Law and Justice Guidelines]

practiceQuestions.q: What is the standard tenure of each Law Commission constituted in independent India?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Law Commission of India is typically reconstituted every three years by the Union Government to undertake legal research and review existing laws. [Primary Reference: Executive Resolution of Ministry of Law and Justice]

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following bodies administratively houses the Law Commission of India?
opts: Ministry of Law and Justice (Department of Legal Affairs)
practiceQuestions.sol: The Law Commission of India functions as an advisory body to the Ministry of Law and Justice, specifically under the Department of Legal Affairs. [Primary Reference: Department of Legal Affairs, MoLJ]

practiceQuestions.q: Who typically serves as members of the Law Commission of India apart from legal academics and retired judges?
opts: Legal experts, retired judges, and law professors
Active practicing advocates of district courts only
practiceQuestions.sol: The Commission comprises legal experts, retired judges of the Supreme Court or High Courts, and reputed legal academics/professors to provide holistic recommendations. [Primary Reference: Ministry of Law and Justice Notifications]

practiceQuestions.q: Pre-independence Law Commissions in British India were formulated primarily under the recommendations stemming from which major legislative enactment?
practiceQuestions.sol: Section 53 of the Charter Act of 1833 provided for the appointment of a Law Commission to inquire into the jurisdiction, forms, and procedures of courts and laws existing in India. [Primary Reference: Charter Act of 1833 / Constitutional History]

practiceQuestions.q: How many Law Commissions have been constituted in independent India up to the 22nd Law Commission?
practiceQuestions.sol: Up to the recent past, 22 Law Commissions have been constituted in independent India, each contributing crucial reports on legal reforms. [Primary Reference: Law Commission of India Official Portal]

practiceQuestions.q: What is the primary constitutional objective behind constituting the Law Commission of India?
opts: To adjudicate disputes between states and the Centre
To undertake legal research and recommend law reforms to ensure justice and modernization
To draft constitutional amendments directly without parliamentary approval
practiceQuestions.sol: The Law Commission works as an expert body to promote legal reform, simplify laws, identify obsolete legislations, and ensure that the legal system aligns with socio-economic changes and constitutional ideals. [Primary Reference: Ministry of Law and Justice Mandate]

practiceQuestions.q: Why are the recommendations of the Law Commission of India not binding on the Government?
opts: Because it is an advisory, non-statutory executive body
Because its recommendations violate the separation of powers
Because the Supreme Court holds a veto over its reports
Because the Constitution expressly forbids accepting advisory reports
practiceQuestions.sol: Since the Law Commission is an advisory body set up by an executive resolution, its recommendations are not binding on the Government of India, though they carry immense persuasive value for legislative reforms. [Primary Reference: Constitutional Convention & Administrative Law]

practiceQuestions.q: How does the Law Commission assist in the 'sunset' review of laws in India?
opts: By passing executive decrees to abolish outdated taxes
By identifying and recommending the repeal of obsolete, redundant, and archaic laws
By sunsetting the judicial tenure of High Court judges
By rewriting fundamental rights during emergencies
practiceQuestions.sol: One of the critical tasks of the Law Commission is to examine existing laws for their continued relevance and recommend the repeal of obsolete or redundant laws, thereby reducing legal clutter. [Primary Reference: Law Commission Reports on Repealing Obsolete Laws]

practiceQuestions.q: What is the role of references made by the Supreme Court or High Courts to the Law Commission?
opts: Courts can directly order the Commission to rewrite penal codes
Courts often suggest legal reforms in judgments, prompting the Government to refer the matter to the Law Commission
Judges automatically become ex-officio members of the Commission upon making a reference
References are legally binding edicts that override parliamentary statutes
practiceQuestions.sol: Often, while adjudicating matters, courts highlight legislative gaps or inconsistencies, prompting the Union Government to make a reference to the Law Commission for detailed study and reform proposals. [Primary Reference: Supreme Court Judgements & Law Commission References]

practiceQuestions.q: Why was the Law Commission's work considered pivotal during the immediate post-independence nation-building phase?
opts: It formulated the entire Indian Constitution from scratch
It helped harmonize pre-independence colonial laws with the newly adopted democratic Constitution and fundamental rights
It abolished the judicial review powers of the Supreme Court
It replaced all civil laws with customary tribal laws
practiceQuestions.sol: Post-independence Law Commissions under leaders like M.C. Setalvad tackled massive tasks such as reforming judicial administration, civil/criminal procedure, and aligning colonial statutes with constitutional mandates. [Primary Reference: Granville Austin, The Indian Constitution: Cornerstone of a Nation]

practiceQuestions.q: Which Law Commission report famously recommended sweeping changes regarding the introduction of a Uniform Civil Code (UCC) or examined family law reforms extensively?
opts: Consultation Paper on Reform of Family Law (by the 21st Law Commission)
1st Report on the Code of Civil Procedure
10th Report on the Law of Contract
practiceQuestions.sol: The 21st Law Commission of India released a comprehensive 'Consultation Paper on Reform of Family Law' in 2018, examining issues related to personal laws, gender equality, and Uniform Civil Code concepts. [Primary Reference: 21st Law Commission Consultation Paper on Family Law]

practiceQuestions.q: How does the Law Commission engage with the public and stakeholders before finalizing its recommendations?
opts: By conducting mandatory referendums across all polling booths
By issuing consultation papers, inviting public comments, and holding deliberations with experts
By bypassing public input completely to maintain judicial secrecy
Through binding decrees voted on by municipal corporations
practiceQuestions.sol: The Law Commission frequently adopts a consultative approach by publishing consultation papers, drafting questionnaires, and inviting views from jurists, academics, NGOs, and the general public. [Primary Reference: Law Commission Working Methodology Guidelines]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the significance of the 14th Report of the Law Commission titled 'Reform of Judicial Administration'?
opts: It established the Supreme Court of India
It provided a comprehensive blueprint for streamlining judicial administration, backlog reduction, and court management in independent India
It nationalized all law firms in the country
It introduced jury trials across all criminal courts
practiceQuestions.sol: Chaired by M.C. Setalvad, the 14th Report (1958) remains a monumental study on judicial administration, addressing arrears, judicial appointments, ethics, and structure of trial and appellate courts. [Primary Reference: 14th Report of the Law Commission of India]

practiceQuestions.q: Why does the Law Commission often recommend the creation of specialized divisions or tribunals within the judicial architecture?
opts: To increase political interference in judicial matters
To handle complex socio-economic, taxation, and commercial disputes efficiently with domain expertise
To abolish the appellate jurisdiction of High Courts permanently
To reduce the salaries of judges
practiceQuestions.sol: Domain-specific legal issues require specialized knowledge (e.g., intellectual property, tax, environmental laws), which prompts the Commission to recommend specialized tribunals or benches for speedier justice. [Primary Reference: Law Commission Reports on Specialized Tribunals]

practiceQuestions.q: What institutional relationship exists between the Law Commission of India and Parliament?
opts: Parliament directly commands the Law Commission to draft bills
The Government lays the Commission's reports before both Houses of Parliament along with an Action Taken Report (ATR)
Parliamentary approval is needed to appoint members of the Law Commission
The Law Commission functions as a standing parliamentary committee
practiceQuestions.sol: Reports prepared by the Law Commission are submitted to the Ministry of Law and Justice, which subsequently lays them before Parliament along with the Government's Action Taken Report (ATR) regarding implementation. [Primary Reference: Parliamentary Procedure & Rules of Business]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Law Commission of India:
1. It is a statutory body established under an Act of Parliament.
2. The First Law Commission of independent India was established in 1955 under the chairmanship of M.C. Setalvad.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because the Law Commission of India is not a statutory body; it is a non-statutory executive body established by an order of the Ministry of Law and Justice. Statement 2 is correct as the first post-independence Law Commission was set up in 1955 with M.C. Setalvad as Chairman. [Primary Reference: Ministry of Law and Justice / Constitution of India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the historical evolution of Law Commissions in India:
1. The First Law Commission of British India was set up under the Charter Act of 1833.
2. Lord Macaulay was appointed as the chairman of the First Law Commission of British India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The Charter Act of 1833 provided for the Law Commission, and Lord Thomas Babington Macaulay headed it, laying the groundwork for codifying Indian laws like the IPC. [Primary Reference: Charter Act of 1833 / Indian Legal History]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the composition and tenure of the Law Commission of India:
1. The Law Commission is normally constituted for a period of three years.
2. It includes legal experts, retired judges, and law professors as members.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The Law Commission of India is reconstituted every three years and consists of a full-time chairperson, member-secretary, and other expert members from the judiciary and academia. [Primary Reference: Executive Resolution, Ministry of Law and Justice]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the legal status of the Law Commission's recommendations:
1. The recommendations of the Law Commission are legally binding on the Parliament of India.
2. The government is mandated to implement all proposals submitted by the Commission within six months.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are incorrect. The Law Commission is an advisory body; its recommendations are not binding on the government, nor is there any mandatory timeframe or legal compulsion for implementing its proposals. [Primary Reference: Constitutional Law & Administrative Norms]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the 14th Report of the Law Commission:
1. It was titled 'Reform of Judicial Administration'.
2. It was submitted under the chairmanship of M.C. Setalvad.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The 14th Report of the Law Commission (1958), headed by M.C. Setalvad, remains a foundational document providing extensive recommendations on judicial administration and court backlogs. [Primary Reference: 14th Report of the Law Commission of India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the subjects taken up by the Law Commission:
1. It can take up studies suo motu based on contemporary legal challenges.
2. It can examine issues referred to it by the Ministry of Law and Justice or the Supreme Court/High Courts.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The Law Commission possesses the mandate to undertake studies on important legal issues both suo motu (on its own initiative) and upon references made by the Ministry of Law and Justice or superior courts. [Primary Reference: Law Commission Mandate Guidelines]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding pre-independence Law Commissions:
1. Macaulay's Law Commission drafted the Indian Penal Code (IPC) in 1837.
2. Subsequent pre-independence commissions led to the enactment of the Code of Civil Procedure and Criminal Procedure Code.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The First Law Commission under Macaulay submitted the draft IPC in 1837 (enacted in 1860), and subsequent British Indian commissions laid the foundation for civil and criminal procedural codes. [Primary Reference: Legal History of India / Charter Act of 1833]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the interaction of the Law Commission with Parliament:
1. Reports of the Law Commission are presented directly to the President of India without passing through executive channels.
2. The Ministry of Law and Justice lays the Commission's reports before both Houses of Parliament along with Action Taken Reports.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because the reports are submitted to the Ministry of Law and Justice (not directly to the President). Statement 2 is partially inaccurate in practice because while reports are laid before Parliament, Action Taken Reports (ATRs) are not uniformly or systematically submitted for every single Law Commission report, creating a gap in follow-up. [Primary Reference: Department of Legal Affairs, MoLJ Procedures]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the role of the Law Commission in reviewing obsolete laws:
1. It has consistently recommended the repeal of hundreds of pre-independence archaic laws that clutter statute books.
2. Its repeal recommendations automatically cancel laws without requiring parliamentary legislation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct; the Commission has repeatedly recommended clearing out redundant laws (e.g., numerous repeal reports leading to the Repealing and Amending Acts). Statement 2 is incorrect because the Commission's reports are only recommendations; actual repeal requires formal legislation passed by Parliament. [Primary Reference: Law Commission Reports on Repealing Acts]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the institutional continuity of Law Commissions in independent India:
1. There has been an unbroken, continuous chain of Law Commissions functioning without any gaps since 1955.
2. The tenure of each Law Commission is enshrined under Article 307 of the Constitution of India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are incorrect. Statement 1 is false because there have been notable gaps and delays in reconstituting Law Commissions (e.g., delays between the 21st and 22nd commissions). Statement 2 is false because the Law Commission is not mentioned anywhere in the Constitution; it is purely an executive body created by cabinet/government resolution. [Primary Reference: Ministry of Law and Justice Executive Notifications]
